A counter-intuitive suggestion to avoid getting drunk but to prevent harassment about your lacking drinking: cultivate a taste for single malt Scotch whisky.

I frequently have to drink professionally, and the best way I've found to avoid getting drunk when all the people around me are is to drink Scotch.

I've had customers and co-workers pound a half dozen beers and a few rounds of shots, giving anyone who didn't keep up a ton of shit, all why I sipped the same two fingers of expensive Scotch I'd started with. It works because most folks aren't big Scotch drinkers, particularly if you cultivate a taste for the feistier Islays, and if you're drinking what they perceive as being jet fuel they're not watching to see how often you refill your glass. Nobody expects you to rush, in part because bar/restaurant prices for a quality single malt are often ridiculous.

If you're not already a fan, Scotch can take some warming up to, though. Start with sipping your way through a half ounce every now and again at home, with water if you want to ease into it though I prefer it neat myself. With a little practice you will work your way through not hating it, to not minding it, to sort of liking it, to really liking it if you give it time.
